answer.summary:
Both halves answered. Broad modding of content AND rules is already approved, along with skip-and-report. Through existing registration a pack may carry scenes and actions, traits, people and names, work and institutions, policy and effects, geography, roles and rules, news, and compatible artwork. The refusal rule is graded rather than all-or-nothing: an independent unknown contribution is skipped and reported while the valid independent content is kept; unknown OPTIONAL metadata can be ignored with a precise warning when semantics and dependencies are unaffected; a bad semantic value or an unknown REQUIRED condition or effect disables the smallest dependent record or action — explicitly not the cost or condition alone while the reward is retained; and only an uninterpretable root or API, or a genuine security or integrity failure, can require rejecting the whole pack. An intentional override is to be distinguished from an accidental collision. ChatGPT offers a sample player-facing line, marked as illustration: installed usable parts, one job skipped for invalid pay, two others available.

Extended 2026-09-22 15:58Z, answer C12 of ChatGPT's stress-test batch: mod-api-vocabulary-is-two-fields: broad supported content/rule extensions and explicit override, not prose-only mods. Skip/report the smallest coherent invalid independent item. A choice's cost/benefit/preconditions remain one validated transaction: never discard an unsupported cost while granting its reward. No raw host/save access. Actual runtime loader→effect→visible reader→Save/Continue is the proof, not a compile-time pack type.

answer.stillOpen:
Two gaps against what our record asked. It gives the eight registration categories but not the priority order, so which to build first is still ours or lamontae's to decide. And no unsandboxed host or raw-save permission is granted, which bounds the 'rules' half. Note also that nothing in either document addresses this record's own framing that the pack vocabulary is two fields — that is our measurement of the current code, not something ChatGPT confirmed or disputed.

Gates on the C12 extension, its words: "Actual runtime loader→effect→visible reader→Save/Continue is the proof, not a compile-time pack type."

notes: This is filed as a design question, not a bug report. The narrow API is coherent and well validated for what it claims to be; the question is what lamontae wants it to become, and his 'not a small whitelisted vocabulary' instruction cannot be satisfied by adding a few more fields to the same whitelist.
The hard/soft refusal half may be answerable without him. It is a direct application of a rule he has already given, and the only real question is what the player is shown.

Related but deliberately NOT asked here: a mod cannot add a trait for a second, independent reason in the trait registry itself. That is a separate record, so an answer to this one does not read as unblocking traits.

The audit line: everything downstream of an enacted law — the production catalogue boundary, the causal-effects engine, the economy derivations — belongs to the 'What passing a law actually does' lane and is deliberately absent from this record.
question: A content pack may today declare exactly two kinds of thing: scenes and durations. What should the pack vocabulary be instead — which systems must a mod be able to add to for this to count as modder-friendly — and when a pack carries a field the engine does not know, should the engine skip that field with a stated reason and install the rest, or keep refusing the pack whole?

sourcesChecked.source: src/simulation/runtime-content-packs.ts on origin/main at 1c4992e8, RuntimeContentPack and assertRuntimeContentPack
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It establishes the present state beyond doubt but decides nothing about intent. The interface carries kind, api, id, version, title, authority, dependencies, durations and scenes — no other field exists. shape() throws when any key is present that is not in the required or optional list, so the whitelist is enforced rather than merely documented. Measured by feeding the validator packs identical but for one added field: a pack adding a trait, a given name, a job, a policy issue or a place is each REFUSED with 'Content pack has missing or unsupported fields.', while the same pack carrying only scenes and durations is ACCEPTED. The message names no field, so a modder is not told which one was wrong.

It confirms there is no soft-fail layer anywhere above the validator: importContentPack calls parseRuntimeContentPack directly and lets the throw escape, so one unknown field loses the whole pack. It does not say what the fail-soft behaviour should be.

The name is honest about the scope — this API is for ordinary scenes — which suggests the narrowness was a deliberate first step rather than an oversight. It does not say what the second step is, or whether the vocabulary grows field by field or moves to an open shape.

title: What a content pack should be allowed to carry, and how it should refuse the rest
usableAnswer: Two things. First, the list of systems a pack must be able to contribute to for this to be modder-friendly, in priority order, with the ones that can wait named as such — traits, given and family names, jobs, places, policy issues and school names are the candidates the repository's own gaps point at. Second, the refusal rule: for each of an unknown top-level field, an unknown field inside a known record, and a known field carrying a bad value, say whether the engine skips it and installs the rest, or refuses the whole pack, and what the player is told either way. A worked example of the message a player should see would settle it faster than a rule.
whyItMatters: lamontae's standing direction is that the game should be modder-friendly in the way RimWorld and The Sims are, that modders may change content AND rules, and explicitly NOT through a small whitelisted vocabulary. Measured on origin/main at 1c4992e8, the vocabulary is a small whitelist of two field kinds, and the refusal is hard rather than soft. His other standing rule — 'ignore it and say so', unknown content skipped with a stated reason, never refused whole, never silent — is contradicted by the same function. These are the two rules that decide whether the modding story works at all, so the shape has to be decided before anyone extends the format.
